question_text: Was the Roll20 data breach a hack?
answer_text: Yes, by Roll20's own account: an unauthorized third party got into its system on Nov 16 and reached account records. Who did it is not known.
label: Confirmed

question_text: How did the attacker get into Roll20?
answer_text: Roll20's email to users reportedly blames a flaw in a system that handled animated image uploads. Roll20 says that pathway is now fixed.
label: Reported

answer_text: If you got the email, a scrambled (bcrypt) form of your password was involved, not the password itself. Change it, and change it anywhere you reused it.
label: Confirmed

question_text: Was my credit card stolen in the Roll20 breach?
answer_text: No full card numbers were involved, Roll20 says. Some users with a saved card had the last 4 digits exposed, which scammers can use to look convincing.
label: Confirmed

question_text: How do I know if my Roll20 account was affected?
answer_text: Roll20 says it emailed every affected user, and if you did not get an email your account was not involved.
label: Confirmed

question_text: Was the Roll20 breach an AI attack?
answer_text: Roll20 says it believes so, but it has not said why, and no one else has shown it.
label: Not established
what_would_settle_it: Roll20 or an independent investigator publishing how the attack was carried out.
Roll20, law enforcement or a credible researcher naming the attacker, or a verified claim of responsibility.
